target_customer: Fitness consumers at launch, then VR, animation and health developers and brands buying motion capture clothing and an open API
problem: Motion capture and form tracking required expensive suits or studios. Enflux made sensor equipped clothing that tracks body movement for exercise feedback and motion capture.
business_model: Hardware sales of smart clothing (about $249 for a shirt and pants set at Kickstarter launch) plus a platform and open API
product_category: Smart clothing and wearable motion capture

founders.name: Doug Hoang
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2016-03-07) says he previously worked on motion sensors for racing cars and has an engine design background.

founders.name: Elijah Schuldt
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page.

competitors.name: Athos
competitors.what: Smart apparel with sensors for workout muscle tracking
competitors.funding_then: $51 million raised, latest round led by Social Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining flexible sensor garments, wireless sync, motion algorithms and manufacturing for a 2 person team was hard hardware work.

defensibility.rationale: Inertial sensor suits were sold by established motion capture vendors and well funded wearables firms; no data or network moat was evident.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Competing mocap suit makers kept selling inertial suits; Enflux's own outcome is not documented.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2016-03-07) covered the Kickstarter launch of body tracking workout clothing; the YC page lists Hasbro and The Jim Henson Company as customers for the VR and animation use.

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the product at Kickstarter launch in 2016 from TechCrunch, Digital Trends and UploadVR; no source on fan community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage was product focused, with no evidence of brand recall, community or merch.

pivots.to: Motion capture clothing for VR, animation and health via open API
pivots.why: The YC page describes the later positioning; no stated reason

outcome_analysis: Enflux launched a Kickstarter in March 2016 from YC Winter 2016 with a two person team building sensor clothing for fitness and later motion capture. No shutdown notice, cause or date was found; the CEO later joined another fitness company per a Crunchbase snippet, so no failure factors are asserted. A hardware product with funded competitors and little defensibility is the likely backdrop but this is not sourced.
notes: No company website listed in the queue, so no site fetch was possible; a search summary says an archived storefront from 2024 sold a $799 kit, which is unverified. The $120K seed rests on aggregator databases (CB Insights, Tracxn per search summary) and likely reflects the YC deal; the 2018 SKL VC seed rests on one aggregator (Bouncewatch) with no amount. A Kickstarter campaign of about $107.6K with 476 backers appears in one search summary without an opened source, so it is not recorded as a round. Search summaries list Mickey Ferri and Pamela Lee as other founders; no opened source confirms so they are not listed. Founded year unclear (aggregators say 2012 or 2013). Founder education not found.
